translationRepairs: Near the end of the Qianyou era he was made commander of the palace infantry and concurrently military governor of Kuizhou. When the Khitans raided the border he was sent to hold Cazhou with his troops.

Near the end of the Qianyou era he was made commander of the palace infantry and concurrently military governor of Kuizhou. When the Khitans raided the border he was sent to hold Chanzhou with his troops.
澶州 is Chanzhou; Cazhou is an erroneous reading.

At the end of Qianyou he was transferred to commander of the palace foot soldiers and concurrently made military governor of Kuizhou; when the Khitans raided the frontier he was sent to lead troops stationed at Cazhou.

At the end of Qianyou he was transferred to commander of the palace foot soldiers and concurrently made military governor of Kuizhou; when the Khitans raided the frontier he was sent to lead troops stationed at Chanzhou.
澶州 is Chanzhou; Cazhou is an erroneous reading.

When Li Ye and his faction rebelled, the Hidden Emperor of Han secretly ordered Li Hongyi, commander at Cazhou, to move against Yin. Hongyi, fearing failure, instead warned Yin of the plot. Yin and Hongyi together sent envoys to Ye asking Taizu to come to the capital's aid.

When Li Ye and his faction rebelled, the Hidden Emperor of Han secretly ordered Li Hongyi, commander at Chanzhou, to move against Yin. Hongyi, fearing failure, instead warned Yin of the plot. Yin and Hongyi together sent envoys to Ye asking Taizu to come to the capital's aid.
澶帥 is the commander at Chanzhou; Cazhou is erroneous.

When Li Ye and others rose in rebellion, the Han Yindi secretly ordered the Cazhou commander Li Hongyi to plot against Yin; Hongyi feared he could not succeed and instead reported the plot to Yin; Yin and Hongyi together sent men to Ye to ask the Taizu to come to the inner crisis.

When Li Ye and others rose in rebellion, the Han Yindi secretly ordered the Chanzhou commander Li Hongyi to plot against Yin; Hongyi feared he could not succeed and instead reported the plot to Yin; Yin and Hongyi together sent men to Ye to ask the Taizu to come to the inner crisis.
澶帥 is the commander at Chanzhou; Cazhou is erroneous.

When Taizu took the throne, Yin was made military governor of the Tiantxiong army and granted the title of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery, while retaining command of the army as before.
When Taizu took the throne, Yin was made military governor of the Tianxiong army and granted the title of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery, while retaining command of the army as before.
天雄 is Tianxiong; Tiantxiong is a typographical error.

When the Taizu ascended the throne, Yin was appointed military governor of the Tiantxiong army, given the added title of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery, and continued to command the army as before.

When the Taizu ascended the throne, Yin was appointed military governor of the Tianxiong army, given the added title of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery, and continued to command the army as before.
天雄 is Tianxiong; Tiantxiong is a typographical error.

Taizu soon sent Zheng Renhui, commander at Cazhou, to Ye. Yin's second son, a commander of the inner guard, failed to come out to receive him. Renhui had him executed and sent the rest of the family into exile at Deng Prefecture.

Taizu soon sent Zheng Renhui, commander at Chanzhou, to Ye. Yin's second son, a commander of the inner guard, failed to come out to receive him. Renhui had him executed and sent the rest of the family into exile at Deng Prefecture.
澶帥 is the commander at Chanzhou; Cazhou is erroneous.

The Taizu soon ordered the Cazhou commander Zheng Renhui to go to Ye; Yin's second son was a commander of the inner guard and did not come out to meet and pay respects; Renhui executed him and moved his family members to Deng Prefecture.

The Taizu soon ordered the Chanzhou commander Zheng Renhui to go to Ye; Yin's second son was a commander of the inner guard and did not come out to meet and pay respects; Renhui executed him and moved his family members to Deng Prefecture.
澶帥 is the commander at Chanzhou; Cazhou is erroneous.

At the end of the Tongguang era Guo Congqian besieged Emperor Zhuangzong inside the palace. Fujin was then a night-guard officer and fought alone with desperate valor within the walls. When Emperor Mingzong learned of this he was pleased and promoted him to an officer of the Pingsheng army, made him prefect of Ci Prefecture, and appointed him vanguard commander of the northern campaign headquarters.

At the end of the Tongguang era Guo Congqian besieged Emperor Zhuangzong inside the palace. Fujin was then a night-guard officer and fought alone with desperate valor within the walls. When Emperor Mingzong learned of this he was pleased and promoted him to an officer of the Pengsheng army, made him prefect of Ci Prefecture, and appointed him vanguard commander of the northern campaign headquarters.
捧聖 is Pengsheng; Pingsheng is an erroneous reading.

At the end of Tang's Tongguang era, Guo Congqian surrounded Emperor Zhuangzong in the inner palace with troops; Fujin was then a guard officer of the night watch and alone exerted his utmost strength to resist and fight within; later Emperor Mingzong learned of this and praised him, promoting him to an officer of the Pingsheng army, sending him out as prefect of Ci Prefecture, and appointing him vanguard commander of the northern campaign headquarters.

When the main army reached the walls of Hedong, the Khitans encamped between Xin and Dai in support of the enemy. An edict ordered Fu Yanqing, military governor of the Tiantxiong army, to lead the generals to hold Xin Prefecture against them.
